recipes.name: Cottage Cheese Chicken Enchiladas
ingredients_raw: 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - boiled and shredded
1 (7 ounce) can chopped green chile peppers

steps.text: To make the chicken mixture: Heat oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat. Add shredded chicken, onion, and green chile peppers; cook and stir until heated through and lightly browned. Stir in taco seasoning and prepare according to package directions.
To make the cheese mixture: Combine sour cream, cottage cheese, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl; mix until well blended.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

To assemble the enchiladas: Warm tortillas until soft and pliable. Spoon some of the chicken mixture and cheese mixture down the center of each tortilla, then sprinkle with a little Monterey Jack cheese. Roll up and place seam-side down in a lightly greased 9x13-inch baking dish. Spoon any remaining chicken and cheese mixtures over the enchiladas. Pour enchilada sauce evenly over the top, then sprinkle with remaining Monterey Jack cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until cheese is melted and bubbly, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Cottage Cheese Chicken Enchiladas
raw_recipe.description: Cottage cheese lends a lighter texture to chicken and cheese enchiladas, bathed in classic red enchilada sauce.

review.reviewBody: This was a big hit at my house!! I would serve this meal for family and friends. Here are some changes I made based upon other reviews I read and my own taste. 1) Instead of boiling chicken, I bought an herb-roasted chicken from the grocery store. I sautéed the onions and peppers alone and added about 2 tsp. of taco powder at the end. After shredding the hot chicken, I added it to that pan. 2) I put some refried beans in each enchilada. 3) For a beautiful look, I sprinkled the top with sliced black olives. 4) I used about 2 cans of enchilada sauce. Very important! Spray the bottom of the pan and pour some sauce on it before adding the rolled enchiladas. 5) I used flour instead of corn tortillas. I moistened each tortilla with the enchilada sauce before putting it together. (Pour some sauce in a deep bowl and wipe the tortilla on both sides.) This helped keep the enchilada moist and tasty. This is beautiful! Let stand about 5 minutes before serving.

This recipe is great just as written, and I highly recommend it. I've ended up making tweaks over time just to make it faster and adjust it to my family's preferences. I use the meat from 1/2 of a cooked rotisserie chicken. I use a packet of Lawry's chicken taco seasoning mix. I saute the onion in a little butter until its soft, then throw in the diced chilies, the chicken, and the packet of dry seasoning mix. (I skip adding the water etc. on the seasoning package directions). After mixing thoroughly, I add the cottage cheese and some mixed Monterey jack and cheddar (maybe 1 1/2 cups?). I mix it all together and roll about 1/2 c.+ of the chicken mixture up in white corn tortillas. I use either Hatch or El Paso enchilada sauce (2 cans). I've also made this with green enchilada sauce. This dish always gets raves!

Delicious. Pretty much followed to a tee, except pan-fried chicken, then used food processor to shred. In the end, I went with Colby Jack vs Monterrey. Made homemade enchilada sauce and Mexican rice to go along with dish and family loved. Thanks for sharing!

This dish is delicious! I'm giving it four stars as the prep time is longer than 30 minutes. I actually cooked the chicken the day before as I like to use bone-in chicken breasts with skins as they have more flavor. Then I shred the chicken and have that chore out of the way for the next day when it's time to put everything together. I also followed another reviewer's suggestion by dipping each tortilla in the enchilada sauce, so I ended up using two whole cans of the sauce. The recipe rendered 14 tortillas, so I took one full pan and packaged each enchilada separately for the freezer. It makes it easy on those week nights when you can pull one or two out of the freezer. Also, I like this recipe with both corn and flour tortillas.

First time ever making enchiladas! These were fabulous and hubby loved them too. Didn't use taco mix because of salt so used cumin, New Mexico chili powder, oregano and garlic. I drained the cottage cheese as someone else suggested and used burrito size flour tortillas. Also sauced the bottom of the pan and smeared refried beans on the tortillas before adding chicken/cheese mixture. Because I used 1 pound of shredded rotisserie chicken I got 8 large enchiladas and I also made a 9 x 9 pan layered like a lasagna which I froze. These were so good and not rich at all! Also used Mrs. Espy's Enchilada Sauce from this site. Will put this in the rotation.

Family really liked this. I did make some changes to make it go further. I made my own enchilada sauce with chocolate added. I then layered the corn tortillas with the sauce, the cottage cheese and Mexican cheese in a 9x13 casserole dish, baked at 350* until bubbling. Excellent dish!! I normally do not change someone's recipe until I have made it as written, (if I need to add or subtract something) but....I needed to increase the amount at the last minute and needed to change it to fit. Thanks for such a great recipe Annabell !!!

I'm watching my diet right now so I used 2 percent greek yogurt instead of sour cream. I made sure not to overcook the chicken when boiling because when you fold it into the onion and chili mixture you can cook a bit more. I also did not stuff and fold each tortilla...I do it the lazy way and layer the tortillas and place the filling and then repeat... Only placed a bit of cheese on the top and broiled the enchiladas after baking for 25 mins. It was VERY good!

My family loved this. I added a can of drained, rinsed black beans to the chicken mixture. I also added the shredded cheese directly into the cottage cheese mixture to save a step in assembly and used hybrid corn/flour tortillas. Served with pico and guac.

This recipe is awesome as is. I have made it many times. I have added some tweaks along the way. I add a box of instant Mexican rice to the bottom of the casserole. I prepare it per the instructions on the box . I also use green sauce instead of red. I use green onion in place of the regular onion. I have made this with flour instead of corn tortillas. Corn is the best. Shredded pepper jack cheese gives it a little spice. I save time and buy a pulled roasted chicken from the grocery store.

I loved it. Made a nice dinner and lunches the next day. I made it a TexMex lasagna by layering the tortillas with the cottage cheese mixture and taco seasoning and hatch chilies, then shredded rottiserie chicken, then shredded pepper Jack and cheddar cheeses. Top with my salsa roja. Served with sour cream, pickled jalapeños, olives, chopped raw white onion and pico. Just Fabulous. Thank you

I love the combination of ingredients. I’ve made it as is for potlucks and had rave reviews. I don’t roll up as enchiladas. I just layer the tortillas with everything else mixed together. I’ve also added black beans and drained, canned corn and cooked in crockpot. Currently my family is following a very low carb diet. I just mix all the ingredients except the tortillas and bake it in a casserole. Skipping the tortillas reduces the carb count.
I substituted a lot of ingredients (the sauce). Will try again with all ingredients.

Really good! We didn’t have any peppers or onions, so I used dry granulated onion, and green chili powder, along with my standard taco seasoning, and the family plates were wiped clean when they made it to the sink. I’d never cooked with cottage cheese before, but this recipe made me a believer! This one’s going into regular rotation.
This was awesome! I added some oregano and cumin to the cottage cheese mixture for a little more spice…

I had cottage cheese on hand from another dish. I searched any recipe using cottage cheese and came across this one. On top of it, I made red enchiladas sauce from chef John's recipe because last time I wasn't too happy with store bought one. This dish turns out a big success as family love it. Definitely a keeper!

Made these last night. Used way less sauce though and triple cheddar. They turned to be a delightful mix of crispy and soft. 1. Go to your favorite Mexican restaurant and buy a half cup of sauce. 2. 4% Cottage cheese 3. Flour tortillas, 6 inch. 4. Use a standing mixer with paddle attachment to shred chicken. 5. Use the full 1 oz Taco Seasoning packet for the half recipe. You'll end up with 4, and you can freeze 2. Perfect for two people. Before bake shown. Won't let me upload the finished version. Anyway, I'll make it again.

Fantastic recipe. I used flour instead of corn tortillas, but will use corn when I have it on hand. I used my own spices rather than a taco seasoning mix, and used havarti cheese since I had that on hand. Any cheese will do! The cottage cheese inside the enchilada was perfect texture and taste. I used homemade enchilada sauce instead of canned (simple recipe using tomato sauce, paprika and canned chiles). It is a wonderful way to use up cottage cheese and leftover chicken.
Easy recipe and tastes great. I’ve made it multiple times.
We love this recipe. Used only 4 oz of chilies. Too spicy for us with 7. We prefer flour tortillas, but corn is good too!
